current_answer: NLnet’s Open Internet Stack call is open to suitable technical projects until 3 November 2026 at 12:00 CET. A first grant request is EUR 5,000–50,000, but applicants must fit an active fund, release results under open licences, and meet the European-dimension rule where applicable. Restack generally excludes AI-related projects. NLnet’s current policy permits disclosed GenAI assistance in an application with a prompt log, but the issuer advises intended LLM users to wait for a revised policy before submitting.

catalogue_card.question: NLnet’s EUR 5,000–50,000 call is open. Will your project fit?
catalogue_card.text: First Open Internet Stack grant requests are due 3 November 2026 at 12:00 CET. The project must fit a fund and open-licence rules. Restack generally excludes AI-related projects. If you plan LLM use in the application, NLnet advises waiting for its revised GenAI policy before submitting.

summary: NLnet’s next deadline is 3 November 2026 at 12:00 CET; first grant requests are EUR 5,000–50,000.
Applicants need a defined technical project, an active fund fit, open-licensed results, and a European dimension for EU-supported funding.
The current policy allows disclosed GenAI help with a prompt log, but excludes purely AI-generated funded work. NLnet advises intended LLM users to wait for a revised policy.
Restack generally excludes AI-related projects; its published exception needs more than one million active human users and direct relevance to the stack.
uncertainty: NLnet has not published the revised GenAI policy; applicants planning LLM use should check it before submission.
Fund choice, project fit, and European dimension remain applicant-specific.
Individual-grant coverage is not a worldwide inventory.
Microsoft and Cloudflare contradictions remain unresolved.
